book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: It's absurd to deliver hospital unit with parasite, in short

parts.note: to deliver someone from a thing is to rid them of it
the intensive care unit

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of delivering a parasite, briefly, to an intensive care ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is laughable and silly, which is exactly what the answer describes.

clue.text: Programme for meeting that's played for ethnic advantage?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the printed list of runners at a race meeting
second meaning: to play the ... is to exploit racial feeling for gain

explanation.walkthrough: A race meeting is a day of horse racing; the second sense is the idiom 'playing the race card'.
explanation.definitionFit: The same compound names a horse-racing programme and a cynical political tactic of appealing to racial prejudice.

clue.text: In the course of not-quite-expected phone call

parts.note: expected is DUE; not quite means its last letter is dropped
to give someone a ring is to phone them

explanation.surface: A phone call arrives in the middle of something, a little sooner than anyone expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning throughout or at some point within a period of time.

clue.text: Place to learn piano, hosted by French writer

indicators.note: a guest is held inside the host, so the letter goes within the writer's name

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A French author hosts a piano lesson in the place where pupils come to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a university or college, where students study.

clue.text: Canaries include this singer with mechanical performance

parts.note: Mario Lanza, the American tenor
doing something by rote is doing it mechanically, from memory

explanation.surface: Pet canaries chirp along with a singer whose act is purely mechanical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canaries' suggests songbirds next to 'singer', but it means the Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanzarote is one of the Canary Islands, the Spanish archipelago off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Friendly island between Italian and Greek ones towards the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the letters are read from the bottom up
places the single island letter between the two named islands

parts.note: Italian one, i.e. an Italian island: Elba
a Greek island: Kos, also spelt Cos

explanation.surface: A friendly little island sits between Italian and Greek neighbours, a little further north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ones' after 'Italian and Greek' means islands, carried over from 'island'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable people enjoy company and are friendly and outgoing.

clue.text: Swelling rage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an inflamed swelling on the skin
second meaning: to seethe with anger

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest mounting anger; they are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a painful pus-filled lump on the skin and seething with fury.

clue.text: Not a high voice but one with musical sound

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'
the Roman numeral for one
a tone is a musical sound of definite pitch

explanation.surface: A singer whose voice is low still manages a musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The baritone range lies between bass and tenor, a male voice well below the high registers.

clue.text: Collaborating in treatment of Nile fever

indicators.note: the letters of the river's name are worked over into a new order

parts.note: the river's name supplies the letters to be rearranged
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: Doctors work together on treating a fever caught on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in league with someone is to be allied or conspiring with them.

clue.text: Company and City embracing reverse of simple formality

indicators.note: the outer letters hug the reversed word between them

parts.note: NY, New York City

indicators.note: the word for simple is read backwards

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A firm and a city council fall back on simple formality.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony is a formal ritual; standing on ceremony means insisting on formal etiquette.

clue.text: Separate and fix, inserting ends of dowel

indicators.note: those two letters are put inside the word for fix

parts.note: to cure a fault is to fix it

indicators.note: takes just the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of the peg's name

explanation.surface: A carpenter splits a joint, then mends it by pushing in a dowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that curdles separates into curds and whey, so curdle is a verb for splitting apart.

clue.text: Offender going to prison? A liberal one may allow such visits

definitions.note: the definition describes the kind of visit; the answer is the adjective in 'conjugal visits'

parts.note: a con is a convict
jug is slang for prison
taken as written

explanation.surface: A convict is sent down; a lenient prison might allow him private visits from his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' places the offender before the prison, and the definition is the tail of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjugal visits let a prisoner spend private time with a spouse, something a liberal regime may permit.

clue.text: Some womanly arts are turned into wrong behaviour

indicators.note: the run of letters is then read backwards
only some of the letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A disapproving voice claims feminine wiles get turned to wicked ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to stray into error or misconduct, as in 'led astray'.

clue.text: Old friend's a gem

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the 's is short for 'is'

explanation.surface: An old friend is called a real gem.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a precious stone with shifting iridescent colours.

clue.text: might be so tense orbiting and not when heading skywards

definitions.text: might be so tense orbiting and not when heading skywards

parts.note: as can mean so, as in 'as good'

indicators.note: going round, so the word for tense surrounds the other piece

parts.note: taut means tightly stretched or tense

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: nor joins a second negative: 'neither this nor that'

explanation.surface: A space traveller feels the strain in orbit rather than at lift-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue starts in lower case, so its opening words seem lost; the whole clue is read as describing the answer, a space traveller who might feel tense while circling Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A space crew member in orbit could well be nervous, so the clue describes the answer as a whole.

clue.text: You may do this to make food ultimately softer

definitions.meaning: points to an everyday kitchen task done in advance
frozen food is rock hard and softens only once it is thawed

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a cooking tip about tenderising; the joke is that the food starts out frozen solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thawing frozen food out of the freezer leaves it soft enough to cook or eat.

clue.text: Practical designer picking up green igneous sample

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters go upward, so the run is read backwards
a sample is a small part taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth designer collects a piece of green volcanic rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'igneous sample' sounds like the definition, a rock specimen, but the definition is the designer.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineer designs machines and structures with practical, working use in mind.

clue.text: Records office make another attempt to enlist soldiers

indicators.note: to enlist is to take in, so the soldiers go inside the other word

parts.note: to retry is to try again
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A recruiting office tries again to sign up soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A registry is an office where official records such as births and marriages are kept.

clue.text: Artist interrupting mean creature with a venomous barb

indicators.note: the artist breaks into the word for mean

parts.note: stingy means mean with money
RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter breaks off from a nasty animal armed with a poisonous spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish whose tail carries a venomous spine.

clue.text: Cut hard diamonds

parts.note: severe means harsh or hard

explanation.surface: A jeweller cuts very hard diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Severed means sliced right through or detached, a past-tense synonym of cut.

clue.text: Name ship 'Joyce" for example

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
a liner is an ocean-going passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone names a ship after Joyce.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray quotation marks are print damage; the clue points to James Joyce, author of Dubliners.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce was born in Dublin, so he is a native of that Irish city.

clue.text: Phone a message to lover after breakup, time after time

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, a lover once the relationship has ended

explanation.surface: Someone keeps contacting a former partner after the split, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' gives one T and then another; the EX sits between them, so the letters read T, EX, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To text is to send a written message by mobile phone, so phoning a message describes the verb.

clue.text: Goalie who stays fresh?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fruit or food that keeps well

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a goalkeeper who never tires; the question mark flags the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is short for goalkeeper and also names produce that keeps, such as an apple that lasts.

clue.text: Widespread Australian vegetation that may depend on Turkey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: acacia, common across Australia
second meaning: the fleshy flap hanging from a turkey's neck

explanation.walkthrough: 'depend' is used in its old sense of hang down, and 'Turkey' with a capital wants to be the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is an Australian acacia and also the loose skin that dangles from a bird's throat.

clue.text: Leggy model may have this servile agent

parts.note: a model showing off her legs may be wearing a very short skirt
read with the clue's 'have', the skirt is something she has on, which supplies the last two letters

explanation.surface: A long-legged model keeps a fawning assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'a leggy model may have this on': a miniskirt. Split the answer after its fourth letter to see the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a subordinate who obeys a master slavishly.

clue.text: Joint order violated

indicators.note: the letters of the following word are put in a new order

parts.note: this word's eight letters are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: A joint court order has been breached.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a woodworking joint of interlocking wedge-shaped pieces.

clue.text: Fix cracked tureen

indicators.note: a cracked dish is broken, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the soup dish's six letters are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a broken soup tureen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like repair; it is the vet's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a pet is to sterilise it, an informal sense of neuter.

clue.text: Resistance when Russian leader's a controversial Siberian

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
Vladimir Putin; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Opposition stirs when a Russian leader is a divisive Siberian figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin, the Siberian mystic at the Romanov court, was a notorious and divisive figure.

clue.text: Equine cry from horse? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the horse goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Someone hears a horse call out and judges the sound about right.
explanation.definitionFit: A bray is the loud harsh call of a donkey, a member of the horse family.

clue.text: accept whisky in a drop of water for a nostalgic time, perhaps

parts.note: yes is a word of acceptance

indicators.note: the whisky goes inside the teardrop

parts.note: a tear is a drop of water from the eye
rye is an American whiskey

explanation.surface: A tear falls into a glass of whisky as someone grows nostalgic.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means times past, recalled with fondness, so it names a time looked back on wistfully.
